title: Fortune & Glory - Revisiting a Game I Should Have Ranked Higher
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j9lMyW5Emo0

A Patreon poll sent Daniel (@dungeondive) back to **Fortune and Glory: The Cliffhanger Game**, and the revisit turns into a public correction: he ranked it around 29th in his top 50 and now thinks it should sit far higher — possibly above Shadows of Brimstone, which is bigger but far harder to actually get onto a table.

He gives five reasons. The audacity of the premise, first — this is a game about punching Nazis, and his photographer starts allied with the President, whose ability simply deletes an enemy. Second, tension from turn one: in co-op the villains begin already sitting on an artifact, so the tug-of-war for the win condition is live before you've done anything. Third, and to his surprise, brevity — the solo game runs about ninety minutes despite a flow chart he holds up as evidence of its own complexity. Fourth, the sheer volume of globetrotting incident. Fifth, serendipity: a New York auction card collided with a villain event letting the cult secretly buy artifacts at auction, and the two random draws made a story neither could tell alone.

The complaints are real too — exceptions stacked on exceptions, and gold coins used for the victory track while blue coins are currency, which he says is backwards.

----

Daniel publicly re-rates a game after one revisit. Which game climbed most in your estimation the second time around?
